groups.title: Challenge Resources tab (official 2026 challenge page)
groups.note: Checked on 2026-11-14 against the Resources tab of the official challenge page. The team brief listed these as 'team notes'; they ARE the official list.

items.name: NASA Earthdata Search
items.what: Search, discover, visualize, refine and access NASA Earth observation data in the browser.
items.checkedNote: HTTP 200, title 'Earthdata Search'; meta description matches. Listed on the challenge Resources tab under NASA Data & Resources > Earth.
items.usedIn: Its catalogue (CMR) proves data coverage (indicator data_coverage); the site card links each point to Earthdata Search (SRTM, EMIT); SRTM elevation/slope via AppEEARS (pending Earthdata Login)

items.name: NASA Worldview
items.what: An interactive interface for browsing full-resolution, global, daily satellite images, generally available within three hours of observation.
items.checkedNote: HTTP 200, title 'NASA Worldview'. The challenge page links to /index.html, which also returns HTTP 200 'NASA Worldview'. Listed on the Resources tab under Earth.
items.usedIn: Same imagery service (GIBS) as the basemap and card images; the site card opens each point in Worldview

items.name: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)

items.usedIn: LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product read from the PDS Geosciences Node (scripts/fetch_official_extras.py) — coded; values appear after the first run of the script (pending)

items.name: Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars (2026 challenge page)
items.what: The official 2026 challenge page, with Objectives, Potential Considerations and a Resources tab (NASA Data & Resources, and Space Agency Partner Resources from CSA, ESA and JAXA).
items.checkedNote: HTTP 200, H1 'Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars'; page metadata firstPublishedAt 2026-09-17, lastPublishedAt 2026-11-13. Resources tab lists Earthdata Search, Worldview, PDS, LRO, LRO Diviner, CSA RCM, RADARSAT-1, SAR Python Tutorial, Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, ESA Open Science Catalog and JAXA G-Portal. It does not list api.nasa.gov, DONKI, OSDR, RadLab, Trek or the two CSA youth/food pages.

items.name: Judging & Awards Guide
items.what: Explains eligibility for Global Judging, the judging criteria (Impact, Creativity, Validity, Relevance, Presentation, each scored 1 to 5) and the three judging phases.
items.checkedNote: HTTP 200, H1 'Judging & Awards Guide'; sections include 'Eligibility for Global Judging', 'Judging Criteria' and Phases 1-3.

items.name: Project Submission Guide
items.what: Explains how to edit and submit the project page, with field instructions, demo tips, start and end times, and how to get the participant certificate.
items.checkedNote: HTTP 200, H1 'Project Submission Guide'; sections include 'Project Submission Start & End Times', 'Project Page Form Field Instructions', 'Tips for Creating a Project Demo' and 'Submitting Your Project'.

items.name: Participant FAQs (use of AI, called 'Super Intelligence (SI)')
items.what: Participants may use SI (AI) tools such as LLMs, code generators and image tools, but each team's submission must describe how SI tools were used to build the project.
items.checkedNote: HTTP 200. The FAQ entry 'What is Super Intelligence? Can teams utilize it during the hackathon?' says that, per a 2026-09-29 U.S. Executive Order, the terms 'Super Intelligence'/'SI' replace 'Artificial Intelligence'/'AI'. No separate AI-policy page was found; the Judging and Submission guides contain no 'AI' text.
